01.title: Roots
01.headline: Vietnam
01.lead: I2FLabs began as a domestic research lab — a place to prove models, pipelines, and AI-first thinking before they reach production.
01.sub: Một lab nghiên cứu trong nước — nơi thử nghiệm mô hình, pipeline và tư duy AI-First trước khi đưa ra thực địa.

02.title: Lab DNA
02.headline: Research first, operations next
02.lead: We prioritize evidence: benchmarks, reproducibility, and scale paths — not one-off slides or demos.
02.sub: Ưu tiên bằng chứng: benchmark, tái lập được và lộ trình mở rộng — không chỉ slide hay demo một lần.

03.title: How we build
03.headline: Purposeful automation
03.lead: Agents, data, and observability are designed together — less manual glue, more reliability and auditability.
03.sub: Agent, dữ liệu và giám sát được thiết kế cùng nhau: giảm thao tác tay, tăng độ tin cậy và kiểm toán.

04.title: Together
04.headline: Partners & ecosystem
04.lead: The lab is open for collaboration: joint research, rapid prototypes, and clearly scoped delivery.
04.sub: Lab mở cho hợp tác: đồng nghiên cứu, prototype nhanh và triển khai có giới hạn rõ.

research.body: We are building the fundamental layers of autonomous intelligence — a future where machine logic and human ambition converge into a single, automated workflow.

process.intro: A clear pipeline to de-risk AI delivery: align the problem, prove value with prototypes, integrate safely, then observe and improve after go-live.

steps.title: Problem framing
steps.body: Align business goals, available data, compliance constraints, and measurable success criteria before writing code.

steps.title: Evidence-backed prototypes
steps.body: Fast experiments on real data, reproducible benchmarks, and explicit no-go boundaries before scaling scope.

steps.title: Integration & safety
steps.body: Wire pipelines into existing systems: APIs, IAM, logging, human fallbacks, and playbooks for model drift.

steps.title: Observe & improve
steps.body: Track output quality, latency, cost, and UX; iterate in short cycles with an audit trail.

faq.intro: A few questions on Vietnam’s innovation context and how small labs are carving out a new role.

items.q: Why are young labs surfacing more visibly in Vietnam right now?
items.a: A deep engineering bench, lower cost to experiment with GenAI and automation, and growing demand from SMEs for pragmatic AI integration — together creating space for small R&D groups closer to the market than pure outsourcing shops.

items.q: How is a research lab different from a traditional outsourcing team?
items.a: Outsourcing optimizes for fixed specs and timelines; labs often keep an internal agenda (exploration, open code, technical writing) and accept experiment risk in exchange for longer-term product or IP advantage.

items.q: How can a young lab stay solvent while keeping research alive?
items.a: Many combine paid integration work with open tracks (OSS, templates, training) for cash flow and reputation. Clear boundaries between billable and exploratory work help avoid burnout.

items.q: How does the GenAI era change expectations of Vietnamese labs?
items.a: Clients expect faster loops from idea to demo within weeks, but are also more sensitive to risk (hallucinations, data leakage). Labs must speak both product and compliance — not only model accuracy.

items.q: What role does open source play for a small lab?
items.a: It is a hiring channel, learning surface, and low-cost credibility signal. Selective contributions align the lab with global tooling standards instead of rebuilding in isolation.

items.q: Should SMEs partner with a young lab instead of a large vendor?
items.a: It depends on the problem: young labs are often nimble and close to decision-making engineers — great for prototypes and deep integration; large vendors fit when you need SLA, scale, and long contracts. Start small with clear metrics and data ownership.
